timestampRule.rule: Every time field in the produced image is either the canonical source epoch or the ext4 writer time. Any third value is a reject, and any value large enough to be a plausible clock reading is definitionally a wall clock.
timestampRule.why: Stated as a closed set rather than as 'differs from expected', because a closed set cannot be widened after the fact to admit what was produced.

corrections.detectedRatherThanSilent: The successor's timestamp audit runs inside the produce phase and rejects any value outside {0, 1}, so a replica carrying a staged ctime aborts with wall-clock-survived-in-the-image before any comparison. The failure mode is loud. The reason not to dispatch anyway is that the record allows one production pair, not that the result would be misread.

effectOnTheSuccessorValue.restatedPlainly: E2FSPROGS_FAKE_TIME=1 is necessary and is not sufficient. It removes every differing field except the ctime of the 13,448 entries copied from staging.

offsetArithmetic.corroboration: st_mode, st_uid and st_gid are copied to i_mode, i_uid and i_gid in the same straight line, with the high halves of the two ids going to l_i_uid_high and l_i_gid_high. They are no part of the claim, which is what makes them useful witnesses: a base that were wrong by any amount would land the ownership and the mode somewhere they visibly are not.

inodeBuffer.baseEstablishedBy: strh w0, [sp, #0x1a2] stores the link count of 1 set at 0x13d00, and i_links_count sits at inode offset 0x1a. 0x13d04 add x2, sp, #0x188 then passes the same address to ext2fs_write_new_inode and later to ext2fs_read_inode and ext2fs_write_inode.

statBuffer.baseEstablishedBy: add x0, sp, #0x80 -> 0x13974 str x0, [sp, #0x18] -> 0x139e8 ldr x1, [sp, #0x18] -> 0x139f0 bl lstat64@plt. The base is the operand of the instruction that forms the pointer lstat64 fills, so it is read rather than inferred from a field.

offsetArithmetic.why: The walk above was read off a disassembly by hand. A mistyped displacement moves a field without making anything read less plausible -- sp+0xd8 and sp+0xe8 are one character apart and name different times -- so the operands are recorded here and the addresses are recomputed from them by scripts/test_native_shadow_boot_root_disk_determinism_successor_arm64_v1.py rather than trusted as written.

confirmationContract.orderThatWouldApply: Acquiring a candidate is an external download, so the pre-registration would be pushed to a remote branch before the download, and the source lock would gain the candidate as an appended entry with the existing 191 left byte-unchanged.
whatWouldCount: the same read that produced this correction, run against the candidate mke2fs: the staging stat is located from its lstat call site, the inode buffer from its i_links_count store, and the instructions between them are shown to take the pinned time rather than the staged one
the candidate's own libext2fs re-read the way this record's was, since a program fix that its library undoes is not a fix
digests of the candidate binaries recorded beside the sites, as the correction above does
whatWouldNotCount: a release note, changelog entry or upstream commit message asserting reproducible output, with no read of the shipped binary
a produced pair of images that happen to match, which cannot separate a fixed cause from two runs that shared a clock
this record's own reasoning about which version ought to work
confirmationContract.why: The requirement above says a version must be confirmed to exist. Left unsaid, confirming would drift towards reading a changelog and believing it. This says what would have to be read instead, so the confirmation is the same kind of evidence as the finding it answers.

staticNegative.claim: The staging overwrite reads nothing from the ext2_filsys struct, so no value of the successor variable can reach i_atime, i_ctime or i_mtime on this path.
staticNegative.consequence: E2FSPROGS_FAKE_TIME is necessary and not sufficient: it fixes the fields ext2fs_write_new_inode writes, and the overwrite that follows puts the staging file's wall clock back into three of them.
staticNegative.fsRegisterEstablishedBy: x21 is moved into x0 before ext2fs_write_new_inode at 0x13d0c, before ext2fs_read_inode at 0x13d48 and before ext2fs_write_inode at 0x13d6c, and all three take ext2_filsys as their first argument.
staticNegative.howCounted: objdump -d over the window, counting loads whose base register is x21 and, separately, loads at displacement 0xb8 from any base. Both counts are zero.

positiveControl.why: The same binary, the same register and the same displacement read fs->now for the inodes mke2fs creates itself, a few instructions before the window. The zero is therefore a property of this path and not of the search.

window.endsAt: bl ext2fs_write_inode@plt, which commits the overwrite
window.startsAt: the return of ext2fs_write_new_inode, which is the last writer that does honour fs->now

corrections.whatTheOriginalClaimGotRight: Every site it lists is real, and for the superblock, for i_crtime and for the handful of inodes mke2fs creates itself, a fixed non-zero fs->now does reach the field and time() sits behind the zero branch.
corrections.whatTheOriginalClaimGotWrong: It generalised ext2fs_write_new_inode to every inode. For the entries mke2fs copies under -d, set_inode_extra runs afterwards and overwrites i_atime, i_ctime and i_mtime from the staging filesystem's struct stat. fs->now is never read on that path, so the writer time cannot reach it.
corrections.whyItCannotBeSetFromUserspace: utimensat sets atime and mtime only. ctime is written by the kernel on every metadata change, including the utimensat that sets the other two, so a staged file's ctime is the moment staging touched it. Two replicas stage at different moments.
corrections.whyOperatorDecision: Every remaining remedy crosses a line this record or the directive draws: a different e2fsprogs changes the sealed source lock, a post-hoc pass promotes debugfs from inspector to writer, and excluding i_ctime from the comparison relaxes the acceptance criterion. None may be chosen here.
corrections.whyTheFirstPassMissedIt: The first pass read the library, where every time field really is guarded by fs->now, and stopped once every differing field had a site. The overwrite lives in mke2fs itself, after the library has already written a correct value, so reading the library alone cannot show it.

argvNotes.-f: force a full check. Without it e2fsck sees a clean superblock and exits 0 without reading the filesystem, and a pass that checked nothing is close enough to not running to be worthless.

e2fsckContract.why: The predecessor recorded that no filesystem check was run. Byte identity says two images agree; it does not say either one is a well-formed filesystem.

digestsAreNotRestatedHere.why: The pinned packages already carry these bytes. A second copy of a sealed fact can drift from it silently, so the expected digests are derived from the frozen packages at verification time rather than typed into this record.

loaderEvidenceContract.why: The predecessor left 'loader-resolves-only-frozen-libraries' unsettled, because the executor computed the resolved library set and then discarded it. A run whose library provenance is not written down cannot be audited after the fact.

preRegistration.amendForbiddenReason: A pre-registration that can be rewritten after seeing the outcome is not a pre-registration. Follow-up implementation commits may be added to the same branch; this commit's bytes must stay as pushed.
preRegistration.purpose: Freeze the acceptance criteria, the fixed-time design, the loader evidence contract and the read-only filesystem check before any production code is changed, so a later result cannot be judged against a bar written after it.

predecessor.relationship: This record removes the cause that record identified. It does not revise, soften or supersede that record's failure verdict, which stands as written.

retryPolicy.onMismatch: HARD STOP; report; do not produce a third image
retryPolicy.rerunAllowedOnlyWhen: CI infrastructure failed before any artifact was created
retryPolicy.rerunForbiddenWhen: outputs were created and then did not match
retryPolicy.why: Re-rolling until two images agree measures patience, not determinism, and the first mismatch is the finding.

productionReadiness.why: This record allows one production pair and forbids retrying a pair that has produced a result. Dispatching against a cause known to be still present would spend that one attempt on a known outcome.

canonicalSourceEpoch.role: the logical timestamp every staged entry carries into the image; the historical record and the input's own meaning

debugfsMustNotBecomeAWriter.why: Stamping the image after the fact would produce a filesystem whose bytes no single tool accounts for, and would move the writer role to an inspector that v1 sealed read-only.

ext4WriterTime.reason: In this build of libext2fs, 0 is the unset sentinel: fs->now == 0 means 'nobody pinned a time', and every stamping site falls back to time(). 1 is the smallest value that is both non-zero and fixed, so it is the smallest change that makes the pin take effect at all.
ext4WriterTime.role: the value actually handed to the frozen e2fsprogs, which is a separate fact from what the staged inputs mean

forbiddenSubstitutions.why: this build reads no such variable; setting it would look like a fix and do nothing
a clock read at build time is exactly the non-determinism being removed
a number chosen for how it reads is a fact nobody can re-derive later
the sentinel; already falsified by the predecessor record

mechanicalPreVerification.answer: It reaches both, and it reaches every field that differed between the two replicas. Each stamping site loads fs->now from offset 0xb8 and branches on zero; the non-zero path stores that value directly, and time() is reached only through the zero branch.

coverage.claimLimit: This says a fixed non-zero value reaches every field that moved. It does not say the produced images will be identical; only a produced pair says that.
coverage.supersededBy: corrections[0] (staged-inode-ctime-is-not-fs-now). Every key above stays as written; the correction says which of them held and which did not, and why the difference was not visible from the sites listed here.

mechanicalPreVerification.digestsAreNotCopiedHere: These are the same two binaries the predecessor record pins by digest, and that record is bound above by path and sha256. Restating the hex here would create a second copy that can drift from the first without saying so.

time.twoDistinctValuesOnPurpose: The staged inputs carry a logical epoch; the filesystem writer needs a clock. They were the same number before, and that is how a sentinel swallowed one of them unnoticed. They are separate fields now so neither can hide inside the other.
